newsitem.title: USA: Md county exec says plans no property tax increase.
newsitem.headline: Md county exec says plans no property tax increase.

text.p: The top executive of Montgomery County, Md., said he plans no increases in the locality's overall property tax rate for the next two years.
County Executive Douglas Duncan also said late Monday in a state of the county address that he is talking to developers on new plans for refurbishing downtown Silver Spring.
Duncan on Nov 12 announced he terminated a pact with Canadian supermall builder Triple Five Group for construction of a $585 million entertainment center for the area.

"One of the lessons we learned is that bigger is not necessarily better," Duncan said of the mega-mall project. "We are focusing on smaller, cluster development" involving a "mix of retail, housing and possibly offices down the road."

On property taxes, Duncan said, "I do not intend to propose any increase in the overall property tax rate for the next two years." Duncan noted he did not propose such rate increases in his first two years in office.
County voters in November turned down a referendum proposal called the Ficker Amendment that would have required county officials to cut income or property taxes.

By contrast, voters in adjoining Prince George's County refused to appeal a 1978 property tax called TRIM, Tax Reform Initiative by Marylanders. On top of that, county voters approved a measure that mandates voter approval of all new taxes.
Duncan also announced he plans to recommend creation of an county inspector general to audit and "better scrutinize" county government operations.
